value.title: Send to a role, the role queue and reply modes
value.summary: Roadmap 001 s05: `pij send role:<id>[/<instance>]` resolves to exactly one live holder through the directory, queues when there is none and wakes the PA, refuses with a list when there are several, and stores the requester's reply mode.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: Delivers req-07 and the request half of req-08 (the notify half is s06). Rulings: C1 (the directory is the authority for role: addressing; if it disagrees with seat_roles the send refuses with a named mismatch), C2 (an --fyi send to a role with no holder still queues and wakes the PA, else the prime), C3 (the role-send receipt prints the request id, which s06's `pij output --answers` uses), C4 (`--reply wake` to a cold requester is an audited forced wake, as the PA watchdog does), C6 (s04's after-assign hook drains the role queue to the new holder).

sections.name: goals
value: Roadmap 001 s05: `pij send role:<id>[/<instance>]` resolves to exactly one live holder through the directory, queues when there is none and wakes the PA, refuses with a list when there are several, and stores the requester's reply mode.

sections.name: non_goals
value: Anything another roadmap step owns; see roadmap 001.

value.claim: Resolve. `pij send role:<id>` and `role:<id>/<instance>` resolve through the project's directory holders (s04) to exactly one live seat and deliver as a normal send; the receipt prints the request id (C3). A directory/seat_roles disagreement refuses with a named mismatch (C1).

Queue and wake. With no live holder, the request is stored on the role's queue (migration 0034: requests with role, instance, requester, reply mode, limit, state) and the PA (else the prime) is woken once with runnable next steps: revive the last holder (showing its context size) or assign a fresh seat. An --fyi send queues too (C2). The queue appears in the PA's watchdog feed until cleared; no new timer. pij never starts a seat itself.
Drain on assign (C6). Assigning a holder runs the s04 after-assign hook, which delivers that role's queued requests to the new holder in order and marks them delivered.
Several holders. With two or more live holders on the addressed role and instance, the send refuses and lists them.

Reply modes (req-08, request half). `--reply wake|fyi|none` (default wake) is stored on the request and returned in the receipt; s06 uses it to notify. `--limit <duration>` is stored for s12 (default: the role's default_limit, C5).

Cost (AGENTS.md, resource cost is a correctness property). Sends to a role cost what a normal send costs; queueing is a store write; the PA wake is one delivery; draining on assign is one delivery per queued request. No new timer or poll; the queue rides the existing watchdog round.

Docs and states. In this PR: roadmap s05 goes to complete (plan cell docs/plans/199-send-to-role); req-07 goes to shipped; req-08 goes to in-progress (s06 finishes it); c-send-role goes to shipped. docs/how/pij-rs-api.md documents new verbs and refusals; the skill's verb coverage tables carry them; `just ddocs-check` and `ddocs validate` on the project docs pass; the PR body has a `Delivers:` line.

sections.name: research_context
sections.value: Code to read first: crates/daemon/src/delivery/ (send path), crates/daemon/src/community/ (directory holders from #122 and the after-assign hook), the PA watchdog feed (pa_watchdog), crates/cli send parsing. Migration 0034 is claimed for this plan.

value.risk: Two lanes edit the same CLI wiring or skill files.
value.mitigation: Rebase onto main before the PR; small diffs at the seam; pm-001 orders merges.

sections.name: execution_guardrails
value: Tests use scratch repos and a private daemon; never the live governance branch or the prod daemon.
Builds: your own target or `just shared-build`; CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0; -p scoping; stop under 25 GB free.
No `git add -A`, no `--no-verify`; no node_modules, never symlinked (C25); TS proof is CI on the exact head.
Shared seams (crates/cli wiring, skills/pij): rebase onto main before the PR and keep edits minimal; don't fork the seam.
One push per review round; no pushes after the PR is out for verdicts unless a verdict asks.
